usdRate.sourceName: Daily NK market survey, Pyongyang (informal market rate)
usdRate.note: Informal market rate, down from 71,200 two weeks earlier; the official state rate is not published regularly and is far stronger. Used because prices and savings follow the market rate.

inflation_cpi.note: North Korea publishes no consumer price index; Daily NK market surveys show rice in Pyongyang rising from about 18,000 to 51,700 won/kg between January and October 2026 and the won falling from about 35,000 to 69,200 per dollar.

inflation_projection.sourceName: Daily NK market price and exchange-rate surveys (2026)
inflation_projection.note: With no official CPI and the market won losing about half its value against the dollar in 2026 after years near 8,000 per dollar, 25% a year is a rounded planning figure between the calm and crisis periods.

policy_rate.note: The Central Bank of the DPRK publishes no policy rate.

savings_account_rate.note: No current published rate; Daily NK (Oct 2023) reported provincial bank savings products paying 4% to 9% depending on branch. The 2023 report is older than 2025.

fdr_1y_rate.note: No published rate; Daily NK (Oct 2023) reported 1- to 10-year savings products at 4% to 9% by branch. The 2023 report is older than 2025.

bank_deposit_avg_rate.note: No published average deposit rate; World Bank FR.INR.DPST has no value for North Korea.

sanchayapatra_5y_rate.note: No government savings certificates currently sold to individuals (the 2003 'People's Life Bonds' were a one-off).

tax_bank_interest.sourceName: Taxation in North Korea (Wikipedia, citing the 1974 law 'On Abolishing the Tax System')
tax_bank_interest.note: Personal income taxes were abolished in 1974 and no tax on interest is described; the state raises revenue through enterprise levies and fees. Legal basis dates from 1974 (older than 2025); secondary source.

credit_card_rate_cap.note: No consumer credit card market; the domestic cash cards carry no credit.

equity_return_low.sourceName: No stock market; capped by reported savings rates (4-9%, 2023)
equity_return_low.note: Low case; no local equity market exists and foreign investment is not open to residents.

equity_return_base.sourceName: No stock market; global equity in won terms capped at the reported 4% savings floor plus 4 points
equity_return_base.note: North Korea has no stock exchange; a global index in won would track currency depreciation, but the base is held to the safe-rate cap.

equity_return_high.note: High case reflecting continued won depreciation.

gold_return_low.sourceName: Gold in won terms; Daily NK exchange-rate surveys
gold_return_low.note: Low case if the market won stabilises as it did in 2019-2023.

gold_return_base.sourceName: Dollar gold trend about 5% plus expected won depreciation about 20%
gold_return_base.note: Gold priced in won follows the dollar gold price plus the market won's fall against the dollar.

gold_return_high.sourceName: Gold in won terms; 2026 won depreciation
gold_return_high.note: High case for a repeat of 2026, when the market won roughly halved against the dollar.

fixed_income_return_low.sourceName: Reported provincial bank savings rates 4-9% (Daily NK, 2023)
fixed_income_return_low.note: Low case allows for frozen or unpaid interest and withdrawal limits.

fixed_income_return_base.sourceName: Reported provincial bank savings rates 4-9% (Daily NK, 2023); no tax on interest
fixed_income_return_base.note: Base at the bottom of the reported 4-9% range, since rates vary by branch and access to deposits is unreliable.

fixed_income_return_high.sourceName: Reported provincial bank savings rates 4-9% (Daily NK, 2023)
fixed_income_return_high.note: High case in the middle of the reported range.

life_claim_settlement_rate.note: The state insurer publishes no claim statistics.

insurance_term_premium_table.note: Insurance is a state monopoly; no term life premium rates are published.

health_hospitalisation_cost.note: Health care is officially free; no published figure for actual out-of-pocket costs, which defector surveys say are common.

oop_health_share.note: World Bank SH.XPD.OOPC.CH.ZS and WHO GHED have no value for North Korea.

goal_inflation_health.sourceName: Headline planning inflation (no medical price index)
goal_inflation_health.note: No medical CPI exists, so health costs use the 25% headline planning rate.

goal_inflation_education.sourceName: Headline planning inflation (no education price index)
goal_inflation_education.note: No education CPI exists, so education costs use the 25% headline planning rate.

life_expectancy.sourceName: World Bank WDI SP.DYN.LE00.IN (UN WPP estimate)

life_table_remaining.sourceName: UN World Population Prospects 2024 via Measured World
life_table_remaining.note: Secondary source reproducing UN WPP 2024; ages 60 and 70 and sex breakdown not found (WHO GHO API unavailable).

support_ratio.sourceName: UN WPP 2024 medium variant via PopulationPyramid.net; World Bank SP.POP.DPND.OL
support_ratio.note: 100 / old-age dependency ratio: 18.6 (2025, World Bank), 31.8 (2040) and 41.6 (2065, populationpyramid.net).

retirement_age_default.sourceName: Korea Times (13 May 2026) on North Korea's Labour Law and its 2024 revision
retirement_age_default.note: The 2024 revision raised office workers' pension age to men 63, women 58 (from 60 and 55 under the 1978 Labour Law) and left manual workers and farmers unchanged, so they stay at men 60 (women 55).

retirement_age_government.sourceName: Korea Times (13 May 2026) on North Korea's 2024 Labour Law revision
retirement_age_government.note: Office workers eligible for the state pension: men 63, women 58 (raised from 60 and 55 in 2024).

retirement_return_low.sourceName: Reported provincial bank savings rates 4-9% (Daily NK, 2023)
retirement_return_low.note: Low case allows for unpaid interest or restricted withdrawals.

retirement_return_base.sourceName: Reported provincial bank savings rates 4-9% (Daily NK, 2023); no tax on interest
retirement_return_base.note: Held at the bottom of the reported deposit range, the only safe instrument.

retirement_return_high.sourceName: Reported provincial bank savings rates 4-9% (Daily NK, 2023)
retirement_return_high.note: High case in the middle of the reported range.

retirement_accumulation_return_low.sourceName: Reported savings rates and won-priced gold
retirement_accumulation_return_low.note: Low case for a mix of bank savings and hard assets.

retirement_accumulation_return_base.sourceName: Reported savings rates (4-9%) and won-priced gold
retirement_accumulation_return_base.note: Mix of 4% savings and some gold or foreign currency held as a hedge.

retirement_accumulation_return_high.note: High case where savings are mostly held in gold or dollars as the won falls.

old_age_allowance_monthly.note: No separate non-contributory social pension documented; the only old-age pension found is the work-linked state pension, whose amounts are not published.

public_pension_scheme.sourceName: Korea Times (13 May 2026) on North Korea's Labour Law and its 2024 revision
public_pension_scheme.note: State elderly pension for workers with enough years of work: men from 60 and women from 55 under the 1978 Labour Law, office workers 63/58 since the 2024 revision; amounts, funding and indexation are not published. taxFree because personal taxes were abolished in 1974.

savings_account.note: State and provincial bank savings accounts exist; trust and access are limited.

fdr_1y.note: Provincial banks offer 1- to 10-year savings products (2023 report).

sanchayapatra_5y.note: No retail government bonds on sale.

equity_fund.note: No stock market or investment funds.

gold.note: No legal retail market for gold bars or coins documented.
